_: Narration for video-short. One entry per scene id in ../video-short/index.html.
Written to be understood by someone who joined the team this week: short
sentences, every term defined the first time it is used, no acronym left bare.
Numbers are spelled the way they should be spoken — the speech synthesiser
reads '98.5%' badly. Each line must fit its scene window; build_narration.py
fails loudly with the overrun if it does not, rather than clipping mid-word.
intro: This is Control Center. It takes a business requirement all the way to release.
problem-context: Here is what really happens on a project. One story, three developers. The first pastes the ticket into their A.I. assistant. The second reads a README from two years ago. The third has only the title. Same story, three different contexts. So three different answers.
one-pack: Now the same requirement goes in once, and out comes a set of files. The epic. Four user stories. Twelve acceptance criteria, each a numbered, testable sentence about what done actually means. The architecture. And one failing test for every criterion. All three developers now read the same pack, and all three get it right.
upstream: The work splits into two halves. The first half is upstream: agree what done means. The requirement is read, the design is drawn, the plan is written, and a named human signs it. Every step leaves a file behind, not a conversation.
downstream: The second half is downstream: build until it is provably done. The pack lands on a fresh branch. The developer's agent takes one criterion at a time. Real tests run. A second model reviews the work before any human is asked to look at it.
ide: Here is the developer's side. They say, start working, and the agent creates the branch and stops. They say, plan the next criterion, and it writes a plan for exactly one. Then the developer edits that plan. That edit is the contract, and the agent builds what the file now says, not what it proposed.
screens: This is the real application, not a mock-up. This is Gate One, plan sign-off. Nothing downstream generates, publishes, or runs until a named person clicks. A click is a decision. Typing yes at a prompt is not.
provenance: Every artifact says what made it. Live A.I., rule based, simulated, or human. A deterministic script is never dressed up as A.I., and simulated work is never counted as A.I. work anywhere.
evidence: And it runs. One requirement went from intake to a released application overnight. Real repository, real pull request, merged, ninety eight point five percent test coverage.
outro: Governance is the product. Not how much the A.I. writes, but how many places a human has to sign.
